{
  "topic": "Optimizing llama.cpp performance with multiple GPUs",
  "audience": "local LLM enthusiasts",
  "problem_or_goal": "Discussing methods to improve token generation speed in llama.cpp when using multiple GPUs, particularly with mixed hardware.",
  "context": "This discussion is based on an archived user account from May 7, 2025, detailing their experiments with llama.cpp on a system with a 3090 and two 3060 GPUs. The original author explored tensor splitting and row split modes to enhance performance with various models.",
  "motivation": "Understanding how to configure tensor splitting and other settings in llama.cpp can significantly impact performance when running large language models on multi-GPU setups. This question aims to explore these techniques based on the archived observations.",
  "desired_response": "A discussion about the effectiveness of tensor splitting and row split modes in llama.cpp for optimizing performance on multi-GPU systems, referencing the observations made in the source material.",
  "speaker_relationship_to_source": "reader of archived source; no claim of personally running reported tests",
  "facts": [
    {
      "id": "F1",
      "text": "Disabling secondary GPUs (3060s) provided a performance boost for smaller models that fit entirely within the primary GPU (3090).",
      "evidence_quote": "If we disable them, we see a performance boost: from 48 to 82 tokens per second, and from 28 to 48.",
      "status": "source-author report, not independently verified measurement"
    },
    {
      "id": "F2",
      "text": "Adjusting tensor split values is necessary for larger models that exceed a single GPU's VRAM, with optimal settings requiring experimentation.",
      "evidence_quote": "we can control how the tensors are split. For example, we can allocate more memory on the first card and less on the second and third.",
      "status": "source-author report, not independently verified measurement"
    },
    {
      "id": "F3",
      "text": "Experimenting with tensor splitting on Qwen3 32B improved performance from 13.0 to 15.6 tokens per second, and further to 16.4 tokens per second with 'row' split mode.",
      "evidence_quote": "We can improve performance from the default 13.0 tokens per second to 15.6 by adjusting the tensor split.",
      "status": "source-author report, not independently verified measurement"
    },
    {
      "id": "F4",
      "text": "Tuning tensor splits for Nemotron 49B (Q6) increased performance from 12.4 to 14.1 tokens per second.",
      "evidence_quote": "With some tuning, we can go from 12.4 to 14.1 tokens per second.",
      "status": "source-author report, not independently verified measurement"
    },
    {
      "id": "F5",
      "text": "For Gemma3 27B, optimized tensor splits boosted performance from 14.9 to 18.9 tokens per second, though 'sm' row mode slightly reduced speed.",
      "evidence_quote": "With optimized tensor split values, we boost performance from 14.9 to 18.9 tokens per second.",
      "status": "source-author report, not independently verified measurement"
    },
    {
      "id": "F6",
      "text": "Mistral Small 24B saw performance increase from 18.8 to 28.2 tokens per second with tensor splitting, with 'sm' row mode yielding slightly less.",
      "evidence_quote": "Performance goes from 18.8 to 28.2 tokens per second with tensor split, but again, `sm` row mode reduces it slightly to 26.1.",
      "status": "source-author report, not independently verified measurement"
    }
  ],
  "allowed_claims": [
    "Tensor splitting can be used to manage model VRAM requirements across multiple GPUs.",
    "Different split modes ('row', 'sm') may yield varying performance results.",
    "Experimentation is key to finding optimal tensor split configurations for specific models and hardware."
  ],
  "forbidden_claims": [
    "The reported token-per-second values are universally applicable.",
    "The 'row' split mode is always superior.",
    "Mixing GPUs is inherently problematic.",
    "Specific hardware configurations are guaranteed to achieve these exact results."
  ],
  "essential_limitations": [
    "The specific motherboard and riser configuration are not detailed.",
    "The exact VRAM allocation for each GPU is not specified.",
    "The precise version of llama.cpp used is not stated, only that it was recent.",
    "The system's CPU and RAM specifications are not provided."
  ],
  "missing_information": [
    "Detailed VRAM allocation settings for each GPU.",
    "Specific llama.cpp version used for testing.",
    "Full system specifications beyond GPU models."
  ]
}
